title: Frontend Engineer
summary: Build the dashboards and checkout surfaces businesses use to move money, on a team that treats interface latency as a correctness problem.
responsibilities: Ship features across the merchant dashboard, from data-dense tables to onboarding flows
Take interfaces from a rough spec through design review to production
Keep the shared component library healthy as more teams adopt it
requirements: Three or more years writing production JavaScript, most of it in React
Fluency in modern CSS layout and a working knowledge of WCAG
Comfort reasoning about state, caching and network failure in the browser

title: Backend Engineer
summary: Work on the realtime engine, connection pooling and edge functions sitting between Postgres and several hundred thousand projects.
responsibilities: Extend the realtime replication layer and its client protocol
Profile and remove bottlenecks in the connection pooler
Review community pull requests and land your own work in the open
requirements: Strong systems programming background in Rust, Go or C++
Deep familiarity with Postgres internals, replication and query planning
Experience operating async services under real production load

title: Product Designer
summary: Design planning and tracking software for engineering teams who notice every frame of latency and every misaligned pixel.
responsibilities: Own a product area end to end, from problem framing to shipped detail
Design keyboard-first flows that stay fast for people who live in the tool
Prototype interactions in code or Figma before committing to them
requirements: A portfolio of shipped desktop or web software, not only concepts
Command of typography, motion and interaction detail
Ability to hold a strong opinion and change it when the evidence does

title: Senior Design Technologist
summary: Sit between design and engineering, turning canvas interactions and foundational components into code the rest of the product builds on.
responsibilities: Build and maintain the component primitives every product team consumes
Prototype canvas features against the real rendering pipeline
Set the standard for how motion and micro-interaction get implemented
requirements: Five or more years bridging design systems and production frontend
Advanced CSS architecture plus working knowledge of Canvas or WebGL
Track record of shipping interactions that feel considered, not decorative

title: Principal Product Manager
summary: Set direction for the build and deploy platform underneath a large share of the modern web, for customers who read your changelog closely.
responsibilities: Own the roadmap for build infrastructure and deployment workflows
Turn noisy developer feedback into a small number of decisive bets
Write the specs, the launch posts and the deprecation notices
requirements: Demonstrated ownership of a developer platform product
A technical background deep enough to argue with engineers productively
Exceptional written communication — most decisions here happen in docs

title: Growth Marketing Lead
summary: Run acquisition for a product bought by engineers, where the usual playbook of gated ebooks and webinars does not work.
responsibilities: Own self-serve signup growth from first touch to activated team
Design and read multi-channel experiments with real statistical care
Build the attribution model the rest of the company trusts
requirements: Experience marketing to a technical audience
Hands-on SQL and comfort building your own dashboards
A history of experiments that changed a decision, not only a slide

title: Staff Data Engineer
summary: Own the telemetry pipelines behind developer AI tooling, at a volume where a one percent inefficiency is a budget line.
responsibilities: Design streaming and batch pipelines that survive schema drift
Set the data quality and governance standard across teams
Cut query latency on the warehouse tables everyone depends on
requirements: Deep experience with Spark, Kafka and a cloud warehouse
Fluency in Python and SQL, and the willingness to read Scala
Judgement about when a pipeline should be deleted rather than fixed

title: AI Platform Engineer
summary: Keep high-throughput inference endpoints fast and up, for frontier models serving a very large number of concurrent requests.
responsibilities: Build and tune the serving layer in front of model inference
Design caching and batching strategies that hold under burst load
Own on-call for systems where downtime is immediately visible
requirements: Strong backend engineering in Python or C++
Experience running large Kubernetes clusters in production
Working understanding of inference optimisation and GPU scheduling

title: Edge Systems Engineer
summary: Write code that runs in 300-plus cities at once, where a rollout bug is a global incident and a millisecond is a real number.
responsibilities: Extend the Workers runtime and its isolate scheduling
Improve cold start and memory behaviour across the fleet
Design deploys that fail safely at global scale
requirements: Systems programming in Rust or C++ with real production exposure
Solid grounding in TCP, TLS and HTTP internals
Experience with progressive rollout and blast-radius control

title: Design Systems Engineer
summary: Maintain the component and token layer that keeps an extremely flexible product feeling like one coherent thing.
responsibilities: Own the token pipeline from design source to shipped CSS
Build accessible primitives teams can compose without asking you
Track and reduce visual drift across the product surface
requirements: Two or more years on a design system used by multiple teams
Strong CSS fundamentals, including cascade layers and container queries
Patience for API design — components are interfaces too

title: Ledger Engineer
summary: Build the double-entry ledger behind corporate cards and reimbursements, where every row has to reconcile to the cent.
responsibilities: Extend the ledger primitives all money movement writes through
Design reconciliation jobs that catch drift before finance does
Model new card and payment products without forking the core
requirements: Backend experience in Python or Java on transactional systems
Real comfort with Postgres isolation levels and idempotency
Care about correctness in a domain where rounding is a bug

title: Time Series Engineer
summary: Work on the storage and query engine that turns trillions of points into a dashboard rendering before anyone gets bored.
responsibilities: Improve compression and retention in the time series store
Push down aggregations so queries touch less data
Instrument the engine well enough to debug it from its own product
requirements: Experience building or operating a storage or query engine
Strong Go or C++ and a habit of profiling before optimising
Understanding of cardinality and how it ruins everything

title: Junior Frontend Engineer
summary: Your first or second engineering role, on a codebase you can read in public before you ever apply.
responsibilities: Ship scoped improvements to the dashboard with review support
Write documentation for the features you build
Triage community issues and turn good ones into pull requests
requirements: Working knowledge of JavaScript, TypeScript and React
Something you have built and can talk about in detail
Willingness to work in the open, including the parts that go wrong

title: Developer Advocate
summary: Explain the platform to the developers using it, and bring back the parts of their experience nobody internally wants to hear.
responsibilities: Write demos, guides and talks that solve a real problem end to end
Represent developer pain in roadmap conversations with evidence
Maintain example repositories people actually clone
requirements: Enough engineering skill to build the demo yourself
Clear writing and comfortable public speaking
Judgement about when marketing has crossed into overpromising

title: Analytics Engineer
summary: Turn raw product events into models the whole company queries, and be the reason two dashboards finally agree.
responsibilities: Own the dbt models behind activation and retention reporting
Define metrics once and defend the definition
Build tests that fail loudly before a stakeholder notices
requirements: Fluent SQL and production experience with dbt or equivalent
Understanding of dimensional modelling and slowly changing dimensions
Ability to say no to a metric that would not survive scrutiny

title: Product Manager, Billing
summary: Own subscription and usage billing for customers whose own revenue depends on getting the invoice right.
responsibilities: Shape the roadmap for subscriptions, metering and invoicing
Work through tax, currency and compliance edges with legal
Run migrations that move customers without breaking their revenue
requirements: Experience owning a billing, payments or pricing surface
Comfort with the detail — this domain punishes hand-waving
Track record of shipping to enterprise customers

title: Brand Designer
summary: A six-month contract to push the visual identity into places it has not been yet — campaigns, events and product moments.
responsibilities: Extend the identity system into campaign and event work
Art direct photography and motion with outside partners
Hand off assets and rules the in-house team can run with
requirements: A brand portfolio with range beyond one house style
Strong typographic craft and layout instincts
Experience working to a contract scope and delivering on it

title: Machine Learning Engineer
summary: Own training and evaluation infrastructure for frontier models, at the point where research ideas meet very large clusters.
responsibilities: Scale distributed training runs and diagnose them when they stall
Build evaluation harnesses researchers trust enough to act on
Reduce the cost of a training run without changing its outcome
requirements: Deep PyTorch experience including distributed and mixed precision
History of debugging multi-node training failures to root cause
Research literacy — you can read the paper and implement it

title: Support Engineer
summary: First line for customers who are themselves engineers, which means the questions are good and the answers have to be real.
responsibilities: Reproduce and diagnose customer issues, in their environment
Write the docs page that stops the ticket from coming back
Escalate with a clear reproduction, not a forwarded email
requirements: Enough SQL and JavaScript to debug a customer application
Clear written English under time pressure
Patience, and a genuine interest in why something broke

title: Technical Writer
summary: Three days a week on the documentation millions of developers read when something has already gone wrong.
responsibilities: Own a documentation area end to end, including its structure
Test every example you publish against the real product
Cut pages that no longer earn their place in the tree
requirements: Published technical documentation you can point at
Working command of Git and the command line
Ruthlessness about unnecessary words

title: Site Reliability Engineer
summary: Keep a global network healthy, and make the next incident shorter than the last by changing the system rather than the runbook.
responsibilities: Own SLOs for a set of edge services and defend the error budget
Automate the toil out of deploy, rollback and capacity work
Run incident reviews that produce changes, not blame
requirements: Production Kubernetes and infrastructure-as-code experience
Strong Linux, networking and debugging fundamentals
Calm under an active incident

title: Growth Product Manager
summary: Own the path from a first signup to a team that has moved its work over, without adding a single growth dark pattern.
responsibilities: Improve activation for new workspaces with measurable experiments
Find and remove the steps where teams quietly stop
Keep growth work consistent with a product known for restraint
requirements: Experience owning activation or conversion in a self-serve product
Comfort with data — you write your own queries
Taste, and the discipline not to ship the cheap win

title: Data Scientist, Risk
summary: Model fraud and credit risk where a false positive blocks a real business and a false negative costs real money.
responsibilities: Build and monitor risk models in production, not in a notebook
Quantify the trade-off between blocked fraud and blocked customers
Partner with policy teams on decisions that are not purely statistical
requirements: Strong applied statistics and production Python
Experience with imbalanced classification and drift monitoring
Ability to explain a model to someone who will not read the maths

title: Security Engineer
summary: Secure a multiplayer product where documents are shared constantly and the sharing model is the product.
responsibilities: Threat model new features before they are built, not after
Build the guardrails that make the secure path the easy path
Run the vulnerability disclosure programme and close the loop
requirements: Deep application security experience in a web product
Working knowledge of applied cryptography and authorisation design
Ability to advise engineers without becoming a blocker

title: Mobile Engineer, iOS
summary: Make a document editor feel native on a phone, including the part where the network disappears in a lift.
responsibilities: Build editor and navigation features in Swift
Improve offline sync and conflict resolution behaviour
Hold the line on startup time and scroll performance
requirements: Two or more years shipping Swift to the App Store
Experience with local persistence and sync conflicts
Instinct for the small details that make an app feel native

title: Content Marketing Manager
summary: Own technical content for the APAC region, for readers who will close the tab the moment it reads like a brochure.
responsibilities: Plan and commission a technical editorial calendar for the region
Edit engineer-written drafts without draining the substance out
Report on what content actually influenced a pipeline decision
requirements: Experience editing technical content for a developer audience
Understanding of search intent beyond keyword volume
Familiarity with the APAC technology market

title: Engineering Intern, Summer
summary: Twelve weeks with a named mentor, a scoped project and a real deploy at the end of it.
responsibilities: Ship one meaningful project to production over the internship
Take part in code review as both author and reviewer
Present what you built to the team in the final week
requirements: Currently studying computer science or equivalent self-taught depth
Working JavaScript or TypeScript and some React exposure
Curiosity that survives the first hard bug

title: Product Design Intern
summary: A summer on a product team, working the way the full-time designers do, on a problem that has not been solved yet.
responsibilities: Take one product problem from research through to a shipped prototype
Participate in design critique every week
Document what you learned for the team that picks it up
requirements: A portfolio showing how you think, not only what you made
Working knowledge of Figma and prototyping
Openness to critique and a habit of asking why
